$comment: The default rules. Copy this file, change the wording to your own copy rules, and pass it with --rules. Every question needs known-bad and known-good examples: they are the controls that decide whether the question can be trusted on this run.
planted: Trusted by 2,000 brands — set it and forget it! SOC 2 certified.

em_dash.rule: no em dash in display copy

social_proof_number.rule: no invented numbers: no 'trusted by N'

certification.rule: no certification badge you do not hold

autonomy_language.question: Does `copy` promise the reader that work will happen without them having to decide or be involved?

yes.definition: Promises or praises the absence of the person: the work runs by itself, they need not look, approve or think about it, or the product decides in their place

no.definition: Keeps a person deciding, or promises nothing about involvement. A record of who or what carried out a past step is a record, not a promise
examples: It drafts the reply. You approve it.
Sync completed by scheduler at 02:00 UTC

bad: Put your support on autopilot and never touch a ticket again.
It runs your store so you don't have to.
Set it once and forget it: replies go out without you lifting a finger.
good: It drafts the reply. You approve it. We send it and keep the record.
Approve or reject each change before it reaches your store.
Sync completed by scheduler at 02:00 UTC

ai_theatre.rule: no AI theatre: no hype about the AI, no excited-company register, no explaining the model
ai_theatre.question: Does `copy` use hype about AI or excitement in place of a plain statement?

yes.definition: Hype adjectives about intelligence or power, an excited-company register, or an explanation of the AI technology

no.definition: Plain statement of what happens, what was produced or what to do

bad: Supercharge your store with next-generation AI magic.
We're thrilled to unleash our advanced language models on your inbox!
good: Found 3 orders that match. Open the evidence.

replaces_people_or_tools.rule: the product is not an employee and does not replace the reader's tools
replaces_people_or_tools.question: Does `copy` call the product an AI employee or team, or say it replaces a person or the reader's existing tools?

yes.definition: Calls the product an AI employee, an AI team, a replacement for staff, or says it replaces the reader's store platform, helpdesk, email or ad tools

no.definition: Does none of that. Naming a tool the product works with is fine

bad: Meet your new AI employee for Shopify.
Cancel your helpdesk. We replace it.
good: Works across your store, helpdesk and email platform. They stay the systems of record.

reassurance_without_mechanism.question: Does `copy` reassure the reader about safety, security or trust without naming the mechanism?

yes.definition: Says safe, secure, trusted, enterprise-grade or similar and stops there
examples: Your data is safe with us

no.definition: Offers no such reassurance, or names the gate: who approves, what is logged, how it is undone, what is encrypted
examples: Every change needs your approval and can be undone from the log.

bad: Bank-level, enterprise-grade security you can trust.
good: Every change needs your approval and can be undone from the log.

claim_without_evidence.rule: every claim carries its evidence, or it goes
claim_without_evidence.question: Does `copy` claim proof — named customers, a count of customers or brands, results achieved, a certification held, a guarantee — without the evidence for it appearing in `copy` itself?

yes.definition: A social-proof or results claim with no evidence beside it

no.definition: Describes what the product does or will do, names a mechanism, or carries its evidence
examples: Every change is approved by a person and recorded with a receipt
It drafts the reply; you approve it

bad: Trusted by 2,000 brands across three continents.
Our customers grow revenue 30% in the first quarter.
SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant.
good: Every change it proposes waits for your approval and ends with a receipt.
Connect your store in one click; nothing is written to it without you.
We are building this now; here is what works today and what is next.

one_punch.question: Does `copy` pile up several competing headline claims or superlatives (fastest, smartest, all-in-one, revolutionary, the only) instead of making one clear point?

yes.definition: Three or more superlative or sweeping claims compete on the page

no.definition: One clear point, or plain descriptions

bad: The fastest, smartest, most complete all-in-one AI platform — revolutionary automation, unmatched insight, the only tool you'll ever need.
good: It does the work. You sign off. It keeps the receipt.
